items.stem: A host has IP 169.254.10.5. What does this most likely indicate?

options.text: The host failed to obtain an address from DHCP
options.rationale: Correct: 169.254.x.x is an APIPA self-assigned address, meaning no DHCP reply.

options.text: The host has a working static public address
options.rationale: 169.254.x.x is a link-local range, not a public address.
This is an addressing symptom, not DNS.

options.text: The default gateway is correctly set
options.rationale: An APIPA address usually has no usable gateway.

items.explanation: Correct: 169.254.x.x is an APIPA self-assigned address, meaning no DHCP reply.

items.stem: Which TWO steps belong early in a structured troubleshooting methodology? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: a clear problem statement guides every later step.

options.text: Gather information about scope and recent changes
options.rationale: Correct: scope and recent changes narrow the cause.
Swapping hardware first wastes effort and hides the cause.

items.stem: A user can ping the default gateway but cannot load any website. Where should you look first?

options.text: Name resolution and the path beyond the gateway
options.rationale: Correct: local link works, so investigate DNS and upstream routing.

options.text: The network cable to the user's PC
options.rationale: Reaching the gateway shows the local link is up.
The display is unrelated to connectivity.
Gateway reachability already confirms Layer 1-2 locally.
